what_its_for: Methamphetamine (Desoxyn) is a prescription stimulant medicine approved by the FDA. It is used to treat Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in children 6 years and older and adults. It may also be used for short-term treatment of obesity when diet and exercise alone have not worked. This medicine helps improve focus, attention, and behavior by affecting certain chemicals in the brain.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth exactly as your doctor prescribes. You can take it with or without food. Take it early in the day (morning or early afternoon) to help prevent trouble sleeping at night. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablets — swallow them whole. Never take more than prescribed, and do not take it more often than directed. This is a controlled substance, so keep it in a safe place away from others.
dosing: For ADHD: The usual starting dose for adults and children 6 years and older is 5 mg taken once or twice daily. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose by 5 mg each week until the right dose is found. The typical dose ranges from 20 mg to 25 mg per day, divided into two doses. For obesity: The usual dose is 5 mg taken 30 minutes before each meal, but this use is short-term only (a few weeks). Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still early in the day. If it is late in the afternoon or evening, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule the next morning. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this can cause serious side effects including trouble sleeping and increased heart rate.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in a secure, locked location out of reach of children and pets. This medicine has a high risk for misuse and theft. Keep track of how many tablets you have. Dispose of unused medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program in your area.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking this medicine in the late afternoon or evening to prevent insomnia. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine — it can increase the risk of serious side effects. Avoid caffeine-containing drinks (coffee, energy drinks, soda) as they may worsen side effects like nervousness, fast heartbeat, or high blood pressure. Do not take with antidepressants called MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine, selegiline, or tranylcypromine) — this combination can be life-threatening. Wait at least 14 days after stopping an MAO inhibitor before starting this medicine. Do not share this medicine with anyone else — it is illegal and dangerous.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain or shortness of breath, fast or irregular heartbeat, high blood pressure, signs of stroke (sudden numbness, weakness, trouble speaking, or vision changes), new or worsening mental health problems such as hearing or seeing things that are not there (hallucinations), aggression, paranoia, or unusual mood changes, signs of circulation problems such as unexplained wounds on fingers or toes, or seizures. Also call your doctor if you notice decreased appetite or significant weight loss, slow growth in children, or if you feel you may be becoming dependent on the medication or feel unable to stop taking it.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvements in focus and attention within the first 1 to 2 weeks of starting treatment at the right dose. Your doctor may adjust your dose over several weeks to find what works best for you. For obesity treatment, this medicine is only meant for short-term use (a few weeks) alongside a calorie-reduced diet and exercise plan. Talk with your doctor regularly about whether the medicine is working and whether you still need it.
special_populations: Children under 6 years old: This medicine is not approved for use in children younger than 6 years old. Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like increased blood pressure and heart rate. Pregnancy: This medicine may harm an unborn baby and can cause premature birth or withdrawal symptoms in newborns. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: This medicine passes into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Patients with heart problems: Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, irregular heartbeat, or a history of heart attack or stroke, as this medicine may not be safe for you. Patients with a history of drug or alcohol abuse: This medicine has a high potential for misuse and addiction. Tell your doctor about any history of substance use disorders before starting treatment.
